newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MRCB seen aiming for bigger finance role.
newsitem.headline: MRCB seen aiming for bigger finance role.

text.p: Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) is positioning itself to acquire a bigger foothold in the finance sector, analysts said on Thursday.
MRCB said on Wednesday it had received approval from the central bank to enter into negotiations to acquire a stake in stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd

Rashid Hussain is Malaysia's largest institutional stockbroker. It also controls 20.4 percent of banking group DCB Holdings Bhd and has announced it is negotiating to acquire a 75 percent stake in Kwong Yik Bank Bhd, currently held by Malayan Banking Corp Bhd.
MRCB, which is involved in property, broadcasting and publishing, earlier this year sold a 20 percent stake in financial group Commerce Asset Holdings Bhd which was held by a subsidiary.
"After having sold off their stake in Commerce Asset earlier this year, MRCB still wants to have an investment in a banking group," said Fiona Leong, head of research at brokers JM Sassoon.
"It looks as if MRCB sold off its stake in Commerce Asset in order to have a stake in a bigger bank," said Gan Kim Khoon, banking analyst at HSBC James Capel.
Analysts believed that Rashid Hussain's acquisition of Kwong Yik would eventually result in a merger between DCB Holdings' banking arm and Kwong Yik.
The central bank has encouraged smaller banks to merge to better compete in an era of financial services liberalisation. Analysts say Malaysia is "overbanked' with 37 commercial banks.
Officials at MRCB, Maybank and DCB Holdings were unavailable for comment.
Rashid Hussain and Kwong Yik officials on Wednesday declined to comment on the continuing negotiations.
Leong at JM Sassoon said the investment in a merged entity involving DCB Holdings' DCB Bank Bhd and Kwong Yik Bank would have twice the assets and around 1.6 times the profits of Commerce Asset.
MRCB sold off its Commerce Asset stake for 960 million ringgit in September.
"The stake in Rashid would have to be at least 20 percent for it to mean anything if MRCB wants to equity account it into its earnings," said Gan.

Analysts said MRCB may end up paying for the Rashid Hussain stake with proceeds from a rumoured sale of at least part of its stake in a private television broadcasting firm, Sistem Televisyen Malaysia Bhd, better known as TV3.
Stephen Weller, director of strategy at brokers Pesaka Jardine Fleming said MRCB looked set to become a new conglomerate on the lines of Renong Bhd
"While Renong became an infrastructure developing conglomerate, MRCB looks set to become a broadcasting, publishing, property and financial one," Weller added.
